gm: For example, a man who engages in the phenomena of desire, Having made an appointment with a woman and not meeting her, However many discursive thoughts of his mind operate in a single day, The bodhisattva will gain that many eons.

dm: Any bodhisattva who, for many billions of eons, Practices generosity toward Arhats and Pratyekabuddhas and maintains ethical discipline, Cannot match the merit of one who speaks of the Dharma that possesses the supreme perfection of wisdom, Even if that merit from giving and morality were spoken of well.
gm: Even if a bodhisattva, for many thousands of millions of eons, Gives gifts to arhats and pratyekabuddhas and observes ethical discipline, For anyone who teaches the dharma endowed with the supreme perfection of wisdom, Giving and ethical discipline do not bear a fraction of the goodness of that teaching.

dm: Any bodhisattva who meditates on the supreme perfection of wisdom, And having arisen from that, teaches the stainless Dharma, And dedicates that for the sake of beings as the cause of enlightenment— There is no virtue in the three worlds equal to that.
gm: Any bodhisattva who meditates on the supreme wisdom, Arising from that, teaches the untainted dharma, And dedicates that as a cause for awakening for the sake of beings, There is no virtue equal to that in the three worlds.

dm: Know that such merit is also accumulated, and likewise empty, Hollow, insubstantial, and without essence. When one practices the wisdom of the Sugatas in that manner, At the time of practicing, one fully grasps immeasurable merit.
gm: Knowing that merit, too, to be an accumulation and likewise empty, Hollow, baseless, and coreless— If one thus engages in the wisdom practice of the sugatas, While engaging, one fully grasps immeasurable merit.

dm: Knowing that all these dharmas, which the Buddha has thoroughly practiced and clearly taught, Are exhausted as mere expressions, Even if one were to speak of them for many tens of billions of eons, The expanse of phenomena is without exhaustion and without increase.
gm: Spoken by the Buddha, vividly practiced and vividly taught, Knowing all these dharmas to be nothing more than mere expressions, Even if they are expressed for many tens of millions and hundreds of billions of eons, In the dharmadhātu, there is no depletion and no increase.

dm: Whatever is called the perfection of the Victors, Those phenomena are also proclaimed to be merely names. A bodhisattva who dedicates without conceptual arrogance Will not decline and will touch the supreme awakening of a Buddha.
gm: Whatever is called the perfection of the victors, Those dharmas too are fully proclaimed to be merely names. A bodhisattva who fully dedicates without a conceited mind Will without decline touch the supreme awakening of a buddha.

dm: Just as when a lamp is lit, the wick is not consumed by the first encounter with the flame, The wick is not the flame, yet without it, the flame does not burn; The wick is not burned by its final contact with the flame, Just as without that final flame, the wick is not burned.
gm: By the first contact of the burning wick of an oil lamp, The wick is not burned, yet without it, it is not burned. By the final contact of the flame, the wick is not burned, Yet without the final flame, the wick is not burned—just as,

dm: Supreme enlightenment is not reached by the initial mind, Yet without that initial mind, it cannot be reached. Peaceful enlightenment is not attained by the final mind, Yet without that, it is also impossible to attain it.
gm: By the first mind, supreme awakening is not touched, Yet without it, one is not able to touch it. By the final mind, peaceful awakening is not attained, Yet without it, one is not able to attain it.

dm: From a seed, the sprout, flower, and fruit arise; Just as it is not the case that the tree does not exist because the seed has ceased, So too, the initial mind is the cause of awakening; It is not the case that awakening does not exist because that mind has ceased.
gm: From a seed, a sprout, a flower, and a fruit arise, And when it ceases, the tree is not absent there—just as, Likewise, the first mind is also the cause of awakening, And when it ceases, it is not that awakening is absent.

dm: Just as a water jar is gradually filled from the first drop to the last, Little by little, it is completely filled; So too, the initial mind is the cause of supreme enlightenment, And by gradually perfecting virtuous qualities, one becomes a Buddha.
gm: By drops of water, a vase from the first to the last, Is gradually, little by little, fully filled—just as, Likewise, the first mind too is the cause of supreme awakening, Gradually, perfecting white virtues, one becomes a buddha.

dm: While practicing the dharmas of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, They do not touch upon nirvāṇa, yet do not engage in signs; For example, just as a skilled boatman goes back and forth, Without staying on either shore and without remaining in the ocean.
gm: Practicing the dharmas of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, Not touching nirvāṇa and not engaging in signs, Just as a skilled boatman going back and forth, Does not dwell on either shore, nor does he dwell in the ocean.

dm: A bodhisattva practicing in this way has no conceit, thinking, "I will be prophesied by the Ten-Powered Ones and shall reach enlightenment." Thinking, "There is nothing at all here," they have no fear of enlightenment. To practice in such a manner is to practice the wisdom of the Sugatas.
gm: A bodhisattva practicing in this way has no conceited mind thinking, "I Am prophesied by the Ten-Powered One and will touch awakening," Nor do they fear awakening, thinking, "There is nothing at all here"; Practicing in this way is practicing the wisdom of the sugatas.

dm: Seeing the world as a desolate wilderness of paths, famine, and disease, They are without fear and don their armor; Striving constantly until the furthest limits of the future, with supreme understanding, They do not give rise to even a speck of weariness in their minds.
gm: Seeing the paths of the wilderness of the world, along with famine and disease, They are without terror and then put on their armor; Always striving until the final limit and vividly knowing, They do not generate even a speck of dust of a weary mind.

dm: Thus the bodhisattvas practice the wisdom of the Victors; They know that these aggregates are empty and unborn from the very beginning. While not in meditative equipoise, they engage in compassion for the realm of sentient beings, And even during that interval, they never decline from the Buddha-dharma.
gm: A bodhisattva engaging in the victors' perfection of wisdom, Knows these aggregates to be empty from the beginning and unarisen; Without resting in meditative equipoise, they enter into compassion for the realm of beings, And in the meantime, they never decline from the buddha dharmas.

dm: For example, a skillful person endowed with all excellent qualities, Who is powerful, invincible, diligent, and knowledgeable in the techniques of the arts, Who has mastered archery and many other fields of craftsmanship, And who, knowing how to perform illusions, greatly desires the welfare of beings—
gm: For example, a skilled person endowed with all qualities, Powerful, invincible, having made effort, knowing the rites of arts, Who has reached the far shore of archery and many crafts, Knowing how to conjure illusions, intensely desiring the welfare of beings,

dm: Having gathered together his father, mother, and wife, Travels along a wilderness path where many enemies dwell, And there conjures many heroic and courageous men; Just as they then travel in safety and return home once again,
gm: Having fully gathered his father, mother, and wives together, Travels on a wilderness path with many enemies; Then he emanates many brave and courageous men, Travels safely, and returns home again—just as,

dm: Likewise, the skillful bodhisattva also, Generates great compassion for all realms of sentient beings, And having completely transcended the four Māras and even the two levels, Abides in supreme meditative absorption, yet does not touch upon awakening.
gm: Likewise, at that time, a skilled bodhisattva, Generating great compassion for all realms of sentient beings, Having utterly passed beyond the four māras and the two, Dwells in the supreme samādhi and does not touch awakening.

dm: Wind relies upon space, and the mass of water relies upon that. This great earth relies upon that, and living beings rely upon it. Such is the causal basis for sentient beings' engagement in karma; Reflect on the meaning of this: upon what does space abide?
gm: Wind is supported on space, on that is supported the mass of water, On that is supported this great earth, on that are supported living beings; Such is the cause of sentient beings engaging in karma; Think about this meaning of space being a pervasive foundation!

dm: Likewise, a bodhisattva who abides in emptiness, Through aspirations based on the knowledge of sentient beings in the world, Manifests a great variety of diverse activities, Yet does not touch upon nirvana, nor do they remain in emptiness.
gm: Likewise, a bodhisattva dwelling in emptiness, Supported by aspirations knowing sentient beings among wanderers, Demonstrates many various kinds of activities, Does not touch nirvāṇa, and does not dwell in emptiness.

dm: When a bodhisattva who is wise and clear-minded Practices this supreme samadhi of empty peace, During that time, one does not cultivate any signs; Abiding in the signless, one practices peace and utter tranquility.
gm: Whenever a skilled and brilliant bodhisattva Engages in this supreme samādhi of peaceful emptiness, During that time they do not intensely cultivate signs; Dwelling in signlessness, they practice peace and profound peace.

dm: A bird flying in the sky has no fixed station; It does not remain there, yet it does not fall to the ground. In this way, a bodhisattva who practices the gateways to liberation Does not touch upon nirvāṇa, yet does not engage with signs.
gm: For a bird flying in the air, there is no place to abide; It does not abide there, nor does it fall to the ground. Likewise, a bodhisattva practicing in the doors of liberation Does not touch nirvāṇa and does not engage in signs.

dm: For example, a man trained in archery shoots an arrow into the sky, And by successively following it with other arrows, He allows no opportunity for that first arrow to fall to the ground; If that person so desires, the arrow will fall to the ground.
gm: For example, a person trained in archery shoots an arrow into the sky, And by connecting other arrows in succession behind it, Does not give the previous arrow a chance to fall to the ground; If that person wishes, that arrow will fall to the ground.

dm: In this way, those who practice the supreme perfection of wisdom, Acting through wisdom, skillful means, strength, and miraculous powers, As long as their roots of virtue are not yet complete, So long will they not attain that supreme emptiness.
gm: Likewise, engaging in the supreme perfection of wisdom, Thoroughly practicing by means of the power of wisdom, skillful means, and miracles, As long as their roots of virtue are not perfected, For that long they do not attain that supreme emptiness.

dm: For example, a monk endowed with the supreme power of miracles Might remain in the sky and simultaneously display various transformations; He demonstrates walking, moving, lying down, and sitting, And he does not grow weary, nor does he become exhausted.
gm: For example, a monk endowed with the supreme power of miracles, Abiding in space, simultaneously emanates magical creations, Demonstrating walking, pacing, sleeping, and sitting; He has no weariness, and he has no fatigue.

dm: Likewise, the wise bodhisattva, while dwelling in emptiness, Abides without a fixed place, having perfected gnosis and miraculous powers; They display an infinite variety of activities for the sake of sentient beings, And for ten million eons, they feel no weariness or exhaustion.
gm: Likewise, a skilled bodhisattva dwelling in emptiness, Having reached the other shore of pristine wisdom and miracles, does not dwell there, Demonstrates infinite kinds of activities to wanderers; For ten million aeons they have no weariness and no fatigue.

dm: For example, just as someone standing at a great precipice, Holding two parasols in their two hands, leaps into the sky, And having cast their body into the great abyss, They do not fall, but continue to travel for as long as they are there.
gm: For example, a person standing at a great precipice, Holding two umbrellas in both hands, Jumps into the sky and casts their body into the great abyss, Yet will not fall as long as they are traveling there.

dm: Likewise, the wise bodhisattva abides in compassion, Having fully taken up the two umbrellas of skillful means and wisdom; They contemplate all phenomena as empty, signless, and wishless, And without touching nirvana, they also perceive the true nature of phenomena.
gm: Likewise, a skilled bodhisattva dwelling in compassion, Completely holding the two umbrellas of skillful means and wisdom, Realizing that dharmas are empty, signless, and wishless, Does not touch nirvāṇa, yet sees the dharmas.

dm: For example, just as those who desire jewels go to a jewel island, And having found jewels, return home again, They do not live in happiness there as solitary captains, While leaving their circle of kinsmen and friends in misery.
gm: For example, a person desiring jewels, having gone to a jewel island, And having found jewels, returns home again; Just as that merchant does not merely live happily by himself there, And leave his host of relatives and friends unhappy.

dm: So too, the bodhisattva who has gone to the jewel island of emptiness, Having attained the meditative concentrations, faculties, and powers, Does not take delight in merely touching nirvana alone, And does not leave the suffering of sentient beings behind.
gm: Likewise, a bodhisattva who has gone to the jewel island of emptiness, And attained the powers of the faculties of concentration, Does not merely delight in touching nirvāṇa, And leave sentient beings in suffering.

dm: For example, in order to gain knowledge of the route, a merchant seeking profit Travels to whatever cities, towns, or villages lie along the way; He does not remain there, nor does he remain even on the Island of Jewels, And without staying at home, he becomes an expert on the path.
gm: For example, an ambitious merchant, in order to know the routes, Goes to whatever intermediate cities, towns, and villages there are. He does not dwell there, nor does he dwell on the jewel island; The wise one does not dwell at home, but becomes skilled in the path.

dm: Likewise, the brilliant bodhisattva is skilled in all the knowledge and liberations Of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas; He does not abide in those, nor does he abide in the primordial wisdom of a Buddha; He does not abide in the unconditioned; he is one who knows the nature of the path.
gm: Likewise, a brilliant bodhisattva is skilled in all The knowledges and liberations of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; They do not dwell in them, nor do they dwell in the Buddha's pristine wisdom; They do not dwell in the unconditioned, but know the nature of the path.

dm: When, having connected with beings through loving-kindness, He practices the meditative stabilizations of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, It is impossible to designate that he has attained nirvana, Or to designate him as something conditioned; he does not abide anywhere.
gm: Whenever, having bound themselves with love for wanderers, They practice the samādhis of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, Can it be designated that they will attain nirvāṇa, Or that they are conditioned? They have no abiding.

dm: For example, just as the body of a magically conjured person is not invisible, And can be designated even by a name, Likewise, a bodhisattva who practices the doors of liberation Can be designated even by a name.
gm: For example, just as an emanated human body is not invisible, And it can also be designated by a name; Likewise, a bodhisattva practicing in the doors of liberation Can also be designated by a name.

dm: If, having thoroughly inquired about their conduct and faculties, The bodhisattva does not fully demonstrate the dharmas of emptiness and signlessness, Nor explain the dharmas of the irreversible stage, One should understand that such a person has not been prophesied.
gm: If, when completely questioned about their practice and faculties, A bodhisattva, the dharmas of emptiness and signlessness Does not completely teach, and the dharmas of the irreversible stage Does not explain, they should be known as unprophesied.

dm: Teaching of the peak of complete realization
gm: Teaching on the Culminating Clear Realization

dm: The fifth chapter explains the clear realization of the pinnacle. One who does not desire the level of an Arhat, the wisdom of a Pratyekabuddha, Or the three realms, even in a dream, But sees the Buddhas and teaches the Dharma to beings— One should understand that this is the prophecy of non-retrogression.
gm: Chapter Five: Teaching the Clear Realization of the Peak. The stage of an arhat and the pristine wisdom of a pratyekabuddha, And the three realms, they do not desire even in dreams; Seeing the buddhas and teaching the dharma to wanderers, They should be known as irreversible and prophesied.

dm: If, in a dream, one sees sentient beings dwelling in the three lower realms, And in that very moment makes a prayer to cut the continuum of the lower realms, And pacifies a mass of fire through the power of the blessing of truth— One should understand that this is the prophecy of non-retrogression.
gm: In a dream, seeing sentient beings abiding in the three lower realms, In that instant they make aspirations to cut off the stream of the lower realms. Through the blessing of truth, the masses of fire are pacified; They should be known as irreversible and prophesied.

dm: The many spirits and diseases in the human world Are pacified through the blessing of truth by those endowed with benefit and compassion; Yet they remain without conceit and do not give rise to pride— One should understand that this is the prophecy of non-retrogression.
gm: In the human world, there are many bhūta demons and diseases; Possessing benefit and compassion, they pacify them through the blessing of truth. Yet they have no conceit and do not produce pride; They should be known as irreversible and prophesied.

dm: Or if, because they have acquired various blessings of truth, They develop conceit, thinking, "I have been prophesied," Or if they become conceited because other bodhisattvas have received a prophecy, Know that those who abide in such conceit are of small intelligence.
gm: However, if through those various blessings of truth Being accomplished, the conceit arises thinking, "I am prophesied," Or if a bodhisattva is conceited about being prophesied by another, Abiding in conceit, they should be known as having small intelligence.

dm: For when Māra approaches by means of a name, He speaks thus: "This is the name of you, your parents, And your lineage back through seven generations of ancestors; And when you become a Buddha, this will be your name."
gm: Māra, having approached through the basis of names, Speaks thus: "These are the names of you and your parents, And of your lineage up to your seven ancestors, And when you become a Buddha, this will be your name."

dm: "And such will be the nature of your future ascetic discipline and yoga; Your former qualities were also like this," he declares. Any bodhisattva who, upon hearing such words, becomes conceited, Should be known as one of small intelligence who has been instigated by Māra.
gm: "Whatever ascetic practices, vows, and yogas you will possess, Your past qualities and conduct were also like this," he says. Whatever bodhisattva hears such words and becomes conceited, Should be known as fully incited by Māra and having small intelligence.

dm: Even if they frequent secluded villages, cities, mountain caves, And rely upon remote hermitages and forest retreats, A bodhisattva who praises themselves and disparages others Should be known as one of small intelligence who has been instigated by Māra.
gm: Very solitary villages, cities, and mountain valleys, And isolated monasteries and forests, they thoroughly rely upon; But a bodhisattva who praises themselves and deprecates others, Should be known as fully incited by Māra and having small intelligence.

dm: Except for those who constantly dwell in villages, regions, and towns, Striving for awakening and the ripening of sentient beings, And who do not generate the desire for the state of an Arhat or Pratyekabuddha— This is what the Sugata calls the solitude of the [Buddha's] sons.
gm: Constantly abiding in villages, provinces, and towns, Except for striving for awakening to mature sentient beings, They do not produce other desires for arhatship or pratyekabuddhahood; This is taught by the sons of the Sugata as being solitary.

dm: Even if one dwells for many millions of years in a mountain cleft Five hundred yojanas wide and filled with snakes, A bodhisattva who does not understand this solitude Will fall into arrogance and remain in a state of distraction.
gm: Whoever, in a mountain valley of five hundred yojanas, Filled with snakes, abides for many ten millions of years, That bodhisattva who does not know this solitude, Having acquired superior pride, abides in mixture.

dm: A bodhisattva who strives for the benefit of beings and has attained meditative concentration, Powers, faculties, liberations, and absorptions—if one treats them with contempt, Thinking, "This person does not practice in forest isolation," The Victor has declared that such a person dwells within the domain of Māra.
gm: When a bodhisattva striving for the benefit of beings attains dhyāna, Powers, faculties, liberations, and samādhi, If one despises them, thinking, "This is not the conduct of isolated monasteries," The Victorious One says they abide in the domain of Māra.

dm: Whether one dwells in a town or in a forest, If one is free from the mind of the two vehicles and is certain of supreme enlightenment, This is the solitude of those who have entered into the service of beings; Any bodhisattva who feels superior to them has degraded themselves.
gm: Whether abiding in a village or else in an isolated monastery, If free from the minds of the two vehicles and certain of supreme awakening, This is the solitude of those engaged in the benefit of beings; That conceited bodhisattva ruins themselves.

dm: Therefore, those who seek supreme enlightenment, Being wise and possessing intense resolve, should utterly conquer pride; Just as a multitude of the sick rely on a physician for healing, One should rely on a spiritual friend without any distraction.
gm: Therefore, one who seeks holy awakening, A wise one possessing strong intention, having definitely destroyed pride, Just as a multitude of sick people rely on a doctor to be cured, Should rely on spiritual friends without wavering.

dm: Bodhisattvas who have entered the supreme awakening of a Buddha Should rely on the perfections as their spiritual friends. Those who provide such instruction are the ground of accomplishment; Through these two causes, the awakening of a Buddha is swiftly realized.
gm: Bodhisattvas entered into the supreme awakening of a Buddha Should rely on spiritual friends together with the perfections. Those who teach accordingly, this is the stage of accomplishment; By these two causes, they will swiftly realize the awakening of a Buddha.

dm: For all the Victors of the past, the future, and those residing in the ten directions, This perfection is the path; there is no other. This perfection is said to be the clarity, the lamp, the light, And the supreme guide for those who have entered upon supreme enlightenment.
gm: The Victorious Ones of the past, future, and whoever abide in the ten directions, The path of all of them is this perfection, and no other. This perfection is, for those entered into supreme awakening, Explained as the supreme illumination, lamp, light, and teacher.

dm: Just as the perfection of wisdom is empty of intrinsic characteristics, One should understand that all these phenomena are likewise empty of such characteristics. When one thoroughly understands that all phenomena are empty and signless, To practice in such a manner is to practice the wisdom of the Sugatas.
gm: Just as the perfection of wisdom is empty of characteristics, Knowing all these phenomena to be similar to that characteristic, If one thoroughly knows phenomena as empty and signless, Practicing like that is the wisdom practice of the Sugata.

dm: Sentient beings, completely famished, desire food, And those with minds attached to cyclic existence wander perpetually. The two phenomena of "self" and "mine" are unreal and empty; Yet the foolish, by their own doing, tie knots in the sky.
gm: Fully starving sentient beings desire food, and Those possessing a mind attached to saṃsāra constantly wander. Both self and the phenomena of self are unreal and empty; Childish beings themselves have cast a knot in space.

dm: For example, it is like being stricken by poison through the mere perception of suspicion; Even if that poison has not entered the body, one will fall unconscious. Likewise, the childish who claim "I" and "mine," Have the notion of a self, and through unreal conceptualization, are born and die in impermanence.
gm: For example, just as poison aroused by the perception of suspicion, Even if that poison has not gone inside, one will faint; Likewise, childish beings, accepting self and what belongs to self, Perceiving that self, which is not real, constantly are born and die.

dm: It is taught that the way one grasps is the way one is completely afflicted; It is said that when "I" and "mine" are not observed, there is total purification. In this, without anything being defiled or purified, The Bodhisattva realizes the perfection of wisdom.
gm: Just as there is apprehension, so is complete affliction taught; Not apprehending self and what belongs to self is taught as complete purification; In this, without anything becoming afflicted or completely pure, The bodhisattva realizes the perfection of wisdom.

dm: However many sentient beings there are throughout Jambudvīpa without exception, If all of them were to generate the mind of supreme enlightenment, And were to practice generosity for many tens of millions of millennia, And were to dedicate it all as a cause for awakening for the sake of all beings,
gm: However many sentient beings there are in Jambudvīpa without exception, If all of them, having generated the mind toward supreme awakening, Were to give gifts for many tens of millions of thousands of years, And dedicate it all as a cause for awakening for the benefit of beings;

dm: If someone were to diligently apply themselves to the supreme perfection of wisdom, And practice in accordance with it for even a single day, The mass of merit from that giving would not equal even a fraction of this. Therefore, one should always engage in wisdom without distraction.
gm: Whoever visibly strives in the supreme perfection of wisdom, If they conform to it for even a single day, That aggregate of generosity cannot match a fraction of their merit; Therefore, one should always engage in wisdom without wavering.

dm: Yogis who practice the supreme perfection of wisdom, Though they generate great compassion, have no perception of sentient beings. At that time, those wise ones become the objects of offering for all the world; They always make meaningful use of the alms of the country.
gm: The yogi practicing the supreme perfection of wisdom, Even when generating great compassion, has no perception of sentient beings; At that time, the wise one becomes a field of generosity for all beings, And always meaningfully fully enjoys the alms of the realm.

dm: Any bodhisattva who has long been connected to this, In order to liberate beings of the heavens, the human realm, and the three lower realms, And who desires to show the vast path to the realm of beings on the other side, Should day and night apply themselves to the perfection of wisdom.
gm: Any bodhisattva who, for the sake of liberating The sentient beings of gods, humans, and the three lower realms bound here for a long time, Desires to teach the broad path to the other shore to the realm of beings, Should strive in the perfection of wisdom day and night.

dm: Just as a person who finds a supreme jewel they had never found before, Is filled with joy at having found it at another time, If they become careless and lose it immediately after finding it, They will suffer constant longing for the jewel they have lost.
gm: A person who previously had not found a supreme jewel, Finding it at another time, out of joy, If they lose it right after finding it by becoming careless, By losing it, desiring the jewel, they will constantly suffer.

dm: In this way, those who have entered supreme enlightenment should never abandon The yoga of the perfection of wisdom, which is like a precious jewel. Just as one who finds a jewel, takes it up, and wraps it with great care, Will quickly travel on and reach a state of peace.
gm: Likewise, one entered into supreme awakening should not abandon yoga In the jewel-like perfection of wisdom; Having found and taken the jewel, one should thoroughly apply exertion, Swiftly progressing, just as one becomes pacified.

dm: Like the sun, free from clouds and arrayed in a lattice of light rays, Arising to conquer all the dense, pitch-black darkness, It eclipses all fireflies, living beings, and spirits, As well as the hosts of stars and all the light of the moon.
gm: The sun, freed from clouds, possessing a net of light rays, Rises, destroying all dense, dark darkness, And outshines all fireflies, living beings, and creatures, Along with the hosts of stars and light of the moon.

dm: Likewise, the bodhisattva who practices the supreme perfection of wisdom, Dwelling in emptiness and the signless, Having destroyed the dense darkness of views, outshines all worldly beings, Arhats, Pratyekabuddhas, and the many bodhisattvas.
gm: Just so, the bodhisattva practicing the supreme perfection of wisdom, Practicing emptiness and signlessness, The wise one, having destroyed the dense thicket of views, outshines all beings, Arhats, pratyekabuddhas, and many bodhisattvas.

dm: For example, a prince who desires to give away wealth Becomes the foremost of all and is worthy of being highly honored; Even now, he brings joy to many sentient beings; What need is there to mention when he has acquired the means and is established in the kingdom?
gm: For example, a prince who desires the purpose of giving away wealth, Having become the chief of all, is worthy to be visibly approached. Even as he is, he brings joy to many sentient beings; What need is there to mention when he attains the means and abides in sovereignty!

dm: In this way, the bodhisattva who is skilled in the practice of wisdom Bestows the nectar of immortality and brings joy to gods and humans. If even now they strive for the benefit of many sentient beings, What need is there to mention when they are established as Kings of Dharma?
gm: Likewise, the bodhisattva wise in practicing wisdom too, Gives the nectar and pleases gods and humans. Even as they are, they strive to benefit many sentient beings; What need is there to mention when they come to abide as the Dharma King!

dm: At that time, the Māras will be pierced with the thorns of anguish, Distressed, sorrowful, dejected, and weak. Thinking, "How can I make this bodhisattva's mind falter?" They set the directions ablaze and hurl meteors to display terrifying sights.
gm: At that time, Māra becomes afflicted by a thorn, Tormented by sorrow, suffering, mental distress, and weakened. Thinking, "How can the mind of this bodhisattva be made to shrink back?" In order to show terrors, he burns the directions and casts meteors.

dm: However, when those wise ones possess intense resolve, And day and night look toward the supreme meaning of the perfection of wisdom, At that time, their body, mind, and speech move like a bird in the sky; How could the factions of darkness ever find an opportunity against them?
gm: When those wise ones, possessing intense resolve, Behold the supreme meaning of the perfection of wisdom day and night, At that time, their body, mind, and speech move like a bird in the sky; How could the associates of the dark one find an opportunity?

dm: When bodhisattvas fight and quarrel, And harbor mutual discord and angry thoughts, At that time, Māra rejoices and becomes extremely comfortable, Thinking that both are far removed from the primordial wisdom of the Victors.
gm: Whenever bodhisattvas become embroiled in quarrels and disputes, And, disagreeing with one another, possess angry minds, At that time, Māra is joyful and becomes supremely happy, Thinking, "Those two will become distant from the wisdom of the Victorious Ones."

dm: Both are distant and will become like flesh-eating demons; Both will cause their own commitments to degenerate. How can there be awakening for those who are hostile and devoid of patience? At that time, the Māras and their factions will be delighted.
gm: "Those two will become distant, and they will become like flesh-eating demons; Both will cause their own promises to degenerate. How can there be awakening for those who are hostile and devoid of patience?" At that time, the Māras along with their factions will become joyful.

dm: If a bodhisattva who has not received a prophecy Becomes angry and initiates a dispute with one who has received a prophecy, For as many moments as there were of that harsh and flawed state of mind, For that many eons they must once again don their armor from the very beginning.
gm: Whichever bodhisattva who has not obtained a prophecy Gets an angry mind and initiates a dispute with one who has obtained a prophecy, For however many moments of mind possessing the fault of hostility there are, For that many eons, they must don the armor from the beginning anew.

dm: The Buddhas reached awakening through the perfection of patience; Generating mindfulness, thinking, "This mind of mine is not good," One should individually confess and restrain it for the future, And not take delight in it; that is how one trains in this Dharma of the Buddha.
gm: "Buddhas touch awakening through the perfection of patience." Generating mindfulness, thinking, "This mind is not good," Confessing individually and restraining themselves in the future, And not rejoicing, they train in this Dharma of the Buddhas.

dm: When training, one does not make any claims about the training; One does not perceive a trainee or the qualities to be trained in, And does not conceptualize between training and non-training— Whoever trains in this way trains here in these Buddha-qualities.
gm: When training, whoever does not assert any training, And does not observe the trainer or the dharmas of training, And does not conceptualize these two: having trained and not having trained, Whoever trains like that, trains in this Dharma of the Buddhas.

dm: Any bodhisattva who understands this kind of training Will never again suffer a decline in training or become immoral; In order to please the Buddha-dharmas, they train in this, Skilled in the higher training, they train without apprehension.
gm: Whichever bodhisattva knows this training like that, Will never become one with degenerate training or faulty ethical discipline; In order to please the Buddhas, they train in this; They are wise in the higher training and lack apprehension.

dm: In this way, the wise light-makers train in wisdom; They do not give rise to even a single unvirtuous thought. Just as darkness cannot remain in the space before it When it is overwhelmed by the rays of the sun moving through the sky,
gm: The wise light-makers train in wisdom like that; They do not generate even a single non-virtuous mind. Just as, when outshone by the rays of the sun moving in the sky, Darkness does not remain in the space before it.

dm: For those who have trained in the perfection of wisdom, All the perfections are gathered within this. Just as the sixty-two views are contained within the view of the transitory collection, So too, it is taught that all these perfections are contained within this one.
gm: For those who have trained in the perfection of wisdom, All perfections come to be included herein. Just as the sixty-two views are included within the view of the transitory collection, Likewise, these perfections are taught to be included (herein).

dm: For example, when the life faculty ceases, All other faculties, however many there may be, likewise cease. In the same way, for the supreme sages who practice the perfection of wisdom, It is taught that all the perfections are gathered within this.
gm: For example, when the life faculty ceases, All the other faculties, however many there are, cease; Likewise, for the supreme wise ones practicing wisdom, All perfections are taught to be included herein.

dm: Bodhisattvas, being skillful, train in whatever qualities the śrāvakas possess, And likewise, they train in all the qualities of the pratyekabuddhas; Yet they do not abide in them, nor do they develop a longing for them, Thinking, "This is what I must learn," and for that reason they train.
gm: Wise bodhisattvas train in whatever are the qualities of śrāvakas, And similarly all the qualities of pratyekabuddhas; They do not abide in them nor generate desire for them; Thinking, "This is to be trained in by me," therefore they train.

dm: Those who have entered into the supreme, irreversible awakening, Rejoice from the depths of their hearts in the generation of the mind of enlightenment; Though one might find the measure of the three thousandfold world system and Mount Meru by weighing them on a scale, The virtue of such rejoicing is not like that.
gm: Regarding those who have fully entered supreme, irreversible awakening, Rejoicing from the depths of one's heart in their generation of the mind— The Mount Meru of a trichiliocosm could be measured by weighing it on a scale, But the virtue of that rejoicing is not like that.

dm: I also rejoice in the mass of merit of all sentient beings, as many as there are, Who strive for virtue and desire to be of benefit; Therefore, once they have attained the qualities of the Victors, They bestow the gift of Dharma upon the world in order to bring suffering to an end.
gm: Seeking virtue and desiring to benefit however many sentient beings there are, They also rejoice in the heaps of merit of them all; Therefore, having attained the qualities of the Victorious Ones, In order to exhaust suffering, they give the gift of Dharma to the world.

dm: Any bodhisattva who fully understands that all phenomena are non-conceptual, Empty, signless, and free from conceptual proliferation, Does not seek awakening through a dualistic wisdom; That yogi strives in the supreme perfection of wisdom.
gm: Whichever bodhisattva, non-conceptualizing, fully knows all dharmas As empty, signless, and free from elaboration, They do not seek awakening through dualistic wisdom; That yogin exerts themselves in the supreme perfection of wisdom.

dm: Just as the element of space and that space itself do not conflict, And it does not exist as something to be attained by anyone at all, Likewise, the bodhisattva who is skilled in the practice of wisdom Is like space, and practices in a state of total peace.
gm: That realm of space and what contradicts that space Do not exist, and no one has attained them; Likewise, the wise bodhisattvas practicing wisdom Are like space and practice total peace.

dm: In the midst of a crowd, a conjured person does not think, "I must please these people," and yet they perform that very action; Although they are seen displaying various miraculous feats, They possess no body, no mind, and not even a name.
gm: In the midst of people, an illusory person does not think, "I will please these people," yet still pleases them; Though seen to display various miracles, They have no body, no mind, and not even a name.

dm: In the same way, while practicing wisdom, it never occurs to one to think, "Having realized awakening, I shall liberate all beings." Although they display various births and many activities, They practice without conceptualization, just like an illusion.
gm: Likewise, those practicing wisdom never think thus: "Having realized awakening, I will completely liberate beings"; Though they demonstrate taking various births and having many activities, Like an illusion, they practice without conceptualizing.

dm: For example, a phantom buddha performs the deeds of a buddha, Yet not even a trace of pride arises in that performance. Likewise, the bodhisattva who is skilled in the practice of wisdom Displays all activities just like a magical emanation.
gm: For example, an emanation of a Buddha performs the deeds of a Buddha, And in doing so, not even a little pride arises; Likewise, the wise bodhisattvas practicing wisdom Demonstrate all activities like an emanation or an illusion.

dm: Just as a skilled carpenter creates mechanical figures of men and women That perform all kinds of tasks, Likewise, the bodhisattva who is skilled in the practice of wisdom Performs all activities through non-conceptual primordial awareness.
gm: A wise carpenter crafts figures similar to Men and women, and they also perform all activities; Likewise, the wise bodhisattvas practicing wisdom Perform all activities with non-conceptualizing pristine awareness.

dm: To those who practice skillfully in this way, the many hosts of gods Join their palms in reverence and prostrate. All the Buddhas throughout the world systems of the ten directions Likewise utter garlands of praise for their qualities.
gm: To the wise who practice thus, many hosts of gods Join their palms, bow down, and pay homage; And however many Buddhas there are in the world systems of the ten directions, They completely proclaim a garland of praise for their qualities.

dm: Even if all the sentient beings in realms as numerous as the sands of the Ganges Were to be considered as having become Māras, And even if each of them emanated that many more from every single hair, All of them together would be unable to create obstacles for the wise.
gm: However many sentient beings there are in fields equal to the Ganges, If all of them, taking on assumed forms, became Māras, And even if they emanated that many from each and every single hair pore, All of them would not be able to cause hindrances for the wise.

dm: Through four causes, the wise and powerful bodhisattva Is difficult for the four Māras to overcome and cannot be shaken: Abiding in emptiness, never forsaking sentient beings, Acting exactly as one speaks, and possessing the blessings of the Sugatas.
gm: By four causes, the wise bodhisattva possesses strength, Is hard to overcome by the four Māras, and cannot be moved: Dwelling in emptiness, not forsaking sentient beings, Acting as they have spoken, and possessing the blessing of the Sugatas.

dm: When this perfection of wisdom, the Mother of the Tathāgatas, is taught, Any bodhisattva who feels devotion and, with sincere resolve, Applies themselves with effort to its realization, Should be known as one who has entered into omniscience itself.
gm: This perfection of wisdom, the mother of the Tathāgatas, When it is taught, whichever bodhisattva aspires to it, And clearly exerts themselves to accomplish it with sincere intent, That noble one should be known to have entered into omniscience.

dm: It does not abide within the dharmadhātu or suchness; For example, like a cloud in the sky, it abides without a place to abide. A mantra-holder, a sky-traveler without a fixed abode, desiring a place to stay, Through the power of mantra, blesses trees to be endowed with out-of-season flowers.
gm: They do not dwell in the dharmadhātu or suchness, For example, like clouds in space, they dwell without dwelling. A mantra-holder, without a dwelling, moving in space, wishing to dwell, By the power of mantras, is endowed with out-of-season flowers and blesses them.

dm: In that way, the skillful and brilliant bodhisattvas practice; They do not perceive a realizer, nor are the Buddha-dharmas observed. One does not perceive an expounder, nor is one who desires or views the Dharma observed. This is the dwelling of those who seek peace and delight in virtuous qualities.
gm: Practicing thus, the wise and luminous bodhisattvas Do not apprehend awakening or the qualities of a Buddha; They do not apprehend one who teaches, one who desires dharma, or one who sees; This is the dwelling of those who desire peace and delight in qualities.

dm: Apart from the liberation of the Tathāgatas and the Arhats, This state is the dwelling of the Hearers and the Pratyekabuddhas; It is a dwelling in the meditative concentration of peace, endowed with sublime tranquility and bliss, The most supreme and unsurpassed of all such states.
gm: Except for the liberations of Arhats and Tathāgatas, This dwelling, among those of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, This dwelling in peaceful samādhi, supremely peaceful and endowed with bliss, Is the supreme and unsurpassed of all however many there are.

dm: Though birds dwell in the sky, they do not fall; Though fish dwell in the water, they do not suffocate or die. Likewise, through the power of meditative concentration, Bodhisattvas Who have reached the far shore dwell in emptiness but do not pass into nirvāṇa.
gm: A bird dwells in the sky, yet does not fall; A fish dwells in water, yet does not suffocate and die; Likewise, the bodhisattva, by the powers of concentration, Having reached the other shore, dwells in emptiness and does not pass into nirvāṇa.

dm: Those who wish to attain the supreme qualities of all beings, To touch the most marvelous and supreme primordial wisdom of the Buddha, And to bestow the most excellent and holy gift of Dharma, Should rely upon this supreme state of the benefactors.
gm: To go to the supreme qualities of all sentient beings, And to touch the supremely marvelous, supreme Buddha-wisdom, Whosoever desires to give the supreme, holy gift of Dharma, Rely on this supreme dwelling of those who bring benefit!

dm: When the Guides fully describe the trainings, This training is the supreme and unsurpassed among all trainings. Any wise person who wishes to reach the far shore of all trainings Should train in this Buddha-training, the Perfection of Wisdom.
gm: When the Guides fully proclaim this training, It is the supreme and unsurpassed of all trainings however many there are. Whichever wise one desires to go to the other shore of all trainings, Train in this perfection of wisdom, the training of the Buddhas!

dm: This is the supreme treasure of Dharma and the most excellent Dharma treasury; It is the Buddha lineage, the treasury of happiness and joy for all beings. The protectors of the world in the ten directions—those of the past and those yet to come— All arise from this, yet the expanse of reality is never exhausted.
gm: This is the supreme Dharma-treasure and the holy Dharma-treasury; It is the lineage of the Buddhas, the treasury of happiness and joy of beings. The protectors of the world of the past, future, and the ten directions, Though they are born from this, the dharmadhātu does not become exhausted.

dm: Just as all the various trees, fruits, flowers, and forests All emerge and grow perfectly from the earth, Yet the earth is neither exhausted nor increased; It does not decline, it is non-conceptual, and it never tires.
gm: However many trees, fruits, flowers, and forests there are, They all perfectly arise and come forth from the earth; Yet, the earth has no exhaustion and has no increase, Does not diminish, does not conceptualize, and has no weariness.

dm: The Buddha’s heirs, the listeners, the solitary realizers, the gods, And all the various phenomena of happiness and well-being for all beings, All these arise from the supreme Perfection of Wisdom; Yet these wisdoms are also neither exhausted nor increased.
gm: The sons of the Buddha, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and gods, And however many dharmas of happiness and joy of all beings there are, They all arise from the supreme perfection of wisdom, And yet wisdom has no exhaustion and has no increase.

dm: However many sentient beings there are—the lesser, the middling, and the superior— The Sugata taught that they all arise from ignorance. When conditions assemble, the machine of suffering fully emerges; That machine of ignorance neither exhausts nor increases.
gm: However many inferior, middling, and supreme sentient beings there are, The Sugatas have taught that they all arise from ignorance; When conditions come together, the machine of suffering perfectly arises, Yet that machine of ignorance has no exhaustion and no increase.

dm: However many aspects of primordial wisdom, gateways, methods, and roots there may be, All these arise from the supreme Perfection of Wisdom. When conditions assemble, the machine of karma fully emerges; In the Perfection of Wisdom, there is no exhaustion and no increase.
gm: However many approaches to knowledge, methods, and roots there are, They all arise from the supreme perfection of wisdom; When conditions come together, the machine of activities perfectly arises, Yet the perfection of wisdom has no exhaustion and no increase.

dm: Any bodhisattva who, regarding dependent origination, Understands this wisdom to be without birth and without exhaustion, Just as the cloudless sun dispels darkness by radiating its beams of light, Will, by destroying the dense gloom of ignorance, attain the self-arisen state.
gm: Whichever bodhisattva, with regard to dependent origination, Knows this wisdom as unborn and unexhausted, Just as the cloudless sun dispels darkness by emitting rays of light, Having destroyed dense ignorance, will attain the state of the Self-Arisen.

dm: Possessing great power, they also dwell in the four concentrations, Yet they do not rely upon them, nor do they make them a fixed abode. Nevertheless, these four concentrations, along with their respective branches, Serve as the basis for attaining the supreme and most excellent awakening.
gm: Endowed with great power, they even abide in the four dhyānas; They do not rely on them and do not abide in them; Nevertheless, these four dhyānas along with their branches, Become the support for attaining supreme holy awakening.

dm: Those who have attained supreme wisdom and abide in the meditative concentrations Also experience the four sublime formless meditative stabilizations. These concentrations are beneficial for supreme and sublime awakening; Yet, a bodhisattva does not train in them for the sake of exhausting the outflows.
gm: Those who have attained supreme wisdom and abide in the dhyānas, Also experience the four holy formless samādhis; These dhyānas are beneficial for supreme holy awakening, But the bodhisattva does not train to exhaust the defilements.

dm: This is a marvelous and wondrous accumulation of qualities: Abiding in meditative concentration and stabilization, they are without signs. If those who abide therein should have their bodies perish, They will be reborn in the desire realm exactly according to their intentions.
gm: This is the marvelous wonder of accumulating qualities: Having abided in the samādhis of the dhyānas, they have no signs; If the bodies of those who abide in them were to fall apart, They are again born in the desire realm according to their intention.

dm: For example, it is like a person of Jambudvīpa who had never before Reached the supreme city of the gods, but later goes there; Having seen those lands that are fully possessed there, Just as one who returns here does not become attached,
gm: For example, if a man of Jambudvīpa who previously Had not gone to the supreme city of the gods of the divine realm were to go later, Having seen those completely possessed objects, When he returns here, he does not become attached to them;

dm: Likewise, the bodhisattvas who possess supreme qualities, Diligent in yoga and abiding in meditative concentration and absorption, Dwell once again in the desire realm without attachment; Like a lotus in the water, they are not stained by the qualities of the foolish.
gm: Similarly, those who hold the supreme qualities of a bodhisattva, Exerting themselves in yoga and abiding in the samādhis of the dhyānas, Again abide in the desire realm without attachment; Like a lotus in water, they do not abide in the dharmas of fools.

dm: The great beings exist solely to bring sentient beings to maturity, To purify the fields, and to complete the perfections; They do not seek rebirth in the formless realm, thinking That the qualities of enlightenment and the perfections would thereby decline.
gm: The great beings, to completely ripen sentient beings, Act only to purify the realms and complete the perfections; Thinking, "The qualities of awakening and the perfections will diminish," They do not seek birth in the formless realm.

dm: For example, if a person were to find a treasure of precious gems, They would not give rise to a mind of desire for them; Yet, at another time, they would take them all, And having taken them and gone home, they would remain without attachment, just so.
gm: For example, if a man were to find treasures of jewels, But did not generate a mind of desire for them, And at another time he completely took them, Yet having taken them and gone home, he does not become attached;

dm: Likewise, the wise bodhisattva, having attained the fourfold tranquility Of concentration and meditative absorption that bestows joy and bliss, Relinquishes that blissful concentration and the meditative absorptions they have attained, And out of compassion for beings, enters again into the realm of desire.
gm: Similarly, the wise bodhisattva, joy and Having attained the happiness-bestowing four peaceful samādhis of the dhyānas, Lets go of the attainment of the dhyāna samādhis endowed with the bliss of the dhyānas, And endowed with compassion for beings, again enters the desire realm.

dm: If a bodhisattva, while dwelling in meditative absorption and concentration, Should generate a mind that desires the vehicle of the Arhats or Pratyekabuddhas, They have become uncomposed, agitated, and mentally distracted; The Buddha's qualities are completely lost, like a ferryman whose boat has been wrecked.
gm: If a bodhisattva abides in the samādhis of the dhyānas, But generates a mind desiring the vehicle of an arhat or pratyekabuddha, They are not in meditative equipoise, but agitated and their mind is distracted; The qualities of a Buddha completely diminish, like a boatman whose boat breaks.

dm: Furthermore, even though they are intensely engaged with the five sensory qualities— Forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and textures— If they take joy in the Bodhicitta that is free from the vehicles of the Arhats and Pratyekabuddhas, Know that these heroes are always in meditative equipoise.
gm: Moreover, forms and sounds, and likewise smells and tastes, Touches, and the five qualities of desire, even if they exert themselves in these, If they are free from the vehicles of the arhat and pratyekabuddha and delight in the mind of awakening, The hero should be known to be constantly in meditative equipoise.

dm: For the sake of other beings and persons, the bodhisattva of pure intention Applies themselves with diligent exertion to the perfection of perseverance. For example, just as a female slave carrying water is powerless and under the control of her master, So too do the heroic beings proceed under the control of all sentient beings.
gm: For the sake of other sentient beings and persons, the perfectly pure bodhisattva Manifestly exerts themselves and acts in the perfection of diligence; For example, a servant woman drawing water has no power of her own, but is under the power of her master; Similarly, the heroes act under the power of all sentient beings.

dm: Whether they are reviled or even constantly beaten, Just as a female slave does not speak back to her master, Thinking, "This person might even kill me," They are overcome by a mind of extreme terror and fear.
gm: Whether scolded or even constantly beaten, The servant woman does not speak words of reply to her master, But thinking, "Because of this, I will be killed," With an extremely terrified mind, she is overcome with fear.

dm: Likewise, those who have entered the supreme awakening for the sake of enlightenment Should remain as if they were servants to all living beings. From this, they will attain awakening and perfect all virtuous qualities; Just as fire arising from grass and wood consumes that very fuel.
gm: Similarly, those who have entered into supreme awakening for the sake of awakening, Should abide like servants to all beings; From this, awakening is attained and the qualities are completed; Fire arises from grass and wood, and burns them up.

dm: Having abandoned one's own happiness with a mind free of expectations, One should strive diligently day and night for the needs of other sentient beings. Just as a mother would attend to an only child, Remain with a sincere heart, free from any sense of weariness.
gm: Letting go of one's own happiness, with a mind free of hope, Exert yourself day and night for the needs of other sentient beings; Like a mother attending to her only child, Abide without weariness with a resolute intention.

dm: Any bodhisattva who wishes to remain for a long time in cyclic existence, A yogi who perseveres in the welfare of sentient beings and the purification of the realm, If they do not give rise to even a speck of weariness, They possess the perfection of diligence and are never negligent.
gm: Whatever bodhisattva wishes to cycle in saṃsāra for a long time, A yogi exerting themselves for the benefit of sentient beings and purifying the realms, If they do not generate even an atom of a weary mind, They are endowed with the perfection of diligence and are free from idleness.

dm: If unskilled bodhisattvas count out tens of millions of eons, And, perceiving it as a long time, strive for enlightenment with a sense of hardship, They will suffer for a long duration while practicing the authentic Dharma. Such individuals are lazy, and their perfection of diligence declines.
gm: The unwise bodhisattva counts tens of millions of eons; If they perceive them as long, they suffer in accomplishing awakening; When accomplishing the authentic dharma, they suffer for a long time; Their perfection of diligence diminishes and they possess laziness.

dm: From the first generation of the mind set upon supreme enlightenment, Until the attainment of unsurpassed awakening, If one maintains this mental focus for even a single day and night, The wise and clear-minded should be known as having initiated diligence.
gm: From the first generation of the mind for supreme awakening, Up until unsurpassable awakening is attained, If they consider it in their mind as just a single day and night, The radiant wise one should be known as having commenced diligence.

dm: If someone were to say, "Only after demolishing Mount Meru Will you attain supreme enlightenment," and if one then Considers the extent of the weariness that would arise, At that moment, the bodhisattva has become lazy.
gm: If someone says thus: "After destroying Mount Meru, You will attain supreme awakening," If they then generate a weary mind and even think of its magnitude, At that time, the bodhisattva has become lazy.

dm: If, however, one thinks, "What is difficult about such a task?" And develops the thought to reduce Mount Meru to dust in a mere instant, That wise bodhisattva has initiated diligent effort, And will, before long, attain the supreme enlightenment of a Leader.
gm: But if they think, "How difficult is a measure just like this?" And generate the mind to crush Mount Meru to dust in a mere instant, The wise bodhisattva has commenced diligence, And without taking long, they will attain the supreme awakening of a guide.

dm: If, with the thought, "I shall bring all beings to maturity and act for their benefit," One applies oneself with body, speech, and mind, Yet remains dwelling in the perception of a self, one has become lazy; They are as far from omniscience as the earth is from the sky.
gm: Thinking, "Having completely ripened beings, I will act for their benefit," If they exert themselves with body, speech, and mind, Because they abide in the perception of a self, they have become lazy, And they become as far from omniscience as the sky is from the earth.

dm: When they have no perception of a body, a mind, or a sentient being, And having turned back from perceptions, they practice the non-dual Dharma— This is what the Benefactor called the perfection of perseverance For those who desire the supreme, undeterred, and peaceful awakening.
gm: Whenever there is no perception of body, mind, and sentient beings, And having completely turned away from perception, one practices the non-dual dharma, For one who desires the supreme, unwaning, peaceful awakening, This was taught by the Benefactor to be the perfection of diligence.

dm: If they should hear others speaking ill or using harsh words, The wise bodhisattva rejoices, thinking, "This is my happiness." Who speaks, who hears, who [speaks] to whom, and for what reason? One who possesses this supreme perfection of patience is wise.
gm: If one hears abusive and harsh words from others, Thinking, "I am happy," the wise bodhisattva rejoices; Who speaks, who hears, by what, what is it, and for what reason? The wise one is endowed with the supreme perfection of patience.

dm: Any bodhisattva who possesses the excellent quality of patience— Suppose someone were to fill the three thousandfold world system with jewels and offer them to the Knower of the World, To the Buddhas, Arhats, and Pratyekabuddhas; The mass of merit from that giving would not equal even a fraction of this.
gm: Whatever bodhisattva is endowed with the excellent dharma of patience, Compared to someone who fills the three thousandfold world system with jewels and offers them to the Knowers of the World, The Buddhas, arhats, and solitary realizers, That mass of generosity cannot match a fraction of the merit of the former.

dm: The body of one who abides in patience becomes completely pure, Possessing the thirty-two major marks and infinite power; They proclaim the supreme Dharma of emptiness to sentient beings. Wise and patient, they bring joy to the world.
gm: The body of one who abides in patience becomes completely pure; With the thirty-two marks and boundless power and strength, They proclaim the supreme empty dharma to sentient beings; Beings will rejoice in this wise one endowed with patience.

dm: If some being were to take a sachet of sandalwood powder And, with great devotion, apply it to a bodhisattva, While another person sprinkles glowing embers over his head, He should generate a mind that is equal and impartial toward both.
gm: If some sentient being takes a handful of sandalwood And with great respect rubs it on the bodhisattva, While another scatters burning coals on their head, towards both They should generate an equal and even mind.

dm: When the wise bodhisattva has practiced such patience, And dedicates that generation of the mind toward supreme enlightenment, That hero, through patience, surpasses all the world’s Arhats, Pratyekabuddhas, and however many diverse realms of sentient beings there are.
gm: Having practiced patience in that way, the wise bodhisattva, If they completely dedicate that generation of the mind to supreme awakening, The hero, through patience towards the entire world, outshines All arhats, solitary realizers, and the many realms of sentient beings.

dm: One who practices patience should also cultivate this thought: "In the hells, the animal realm, and the world of Yama, there is much suffering. Since I have helplessly experienced harm due to the causes of sensual desire, Why should I not now endure hardship for the sake of enlightenment?"
gm: The one who practices patience should also generate the mind thinking this: "In the hells, animal realms, and the world of Yama, there is much suffering; If one experiences unavoidable harm as a result of sensory pleasures, Why should I not now practice patience for the sake of awakening?"

dm: Whips, sticks, weapons, being killed, bound, or beaten, Decapitation, and the cutting off of ears, feet, hands, and nose— Thinking, "I shall endure whatever worldly sufferings there may be," The bodhisattva abides in the perfection of patience.
gm: "Whips, sticks, weapons, killing, binding, and beating, Severing of the head, and cutting off ears, hands, feet, and nose— Whatever sufferings exist in the world, I will endure them!" Thinking this, the bodhisattva abides in the perfection of patience.

dm: Through ethical discipline, those who desire peace become noble. Abiding in the domain of the ten powers, their ethical discipline never declines. They follow all the various activities of the vows; For the benefit of all beings, they also dedicate them to enlightenment.
gm: Through discipline, those who desire peace become exalted; Abiding in the domain of the ten powers, their discipline does not wane. They engage in all the activities of vows, whatever they may be, And dedicate them to awakening for the benefit of all sentient beings.

dm: If one wishes to attain the awakening of an Arhat or a Pratyekabuddha, One is immoral, unskilled, and one’s conduct has degenerated. But if one fully dedicates toward supreme, peaceful awakening, Even while engaged in sensory pleasures, one abides in the perfection of ethical discipline.
gm: If one desires to touch the awakening of an arhat or solitary realizer, One's discipline is broken, one is unwise, and thus one's conduct degenerates. But if one completely dedicates it to the supreme, peaceful awakening, Even while engaged in sensory pleasures, one abides in the perfection of discipline.

dm: Those qualities from which the virtues of certain awakening arise— This is the meaning of ethical discipline for those endowed with virtuous qualities. The complete degeneration of the awakening of those who perform beneficial dharmas— This is what the Guide has called "immoral conduct."
gm: Whatever dharmas produce the qualities of definite awakening, This is the purpose of discipline for those endowed with virtuous dharmas. Whatever dharmas cause the awakening of benefactors to completely degenerate, This was taught by the Guide to be broken discipline.

dm: Even if a bodhisattva indulges in the five objects of sensory desire, If they have gone for refuge to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the noble Sangha, And maintain the mental orientation toward omniscience, thinking, "I must achieve buddhahood," The wise should understand that they abide in the perfection of ethical discipline.
gm: Even if a bodhisattva enjoys the five sensory pleasures, If they have taken refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and the noble Sangha, And direct their mind toward omniscience, thinking, "I will accomplish buddhahood!" The wise one should be known as abiding in the perfection of discipline.

dm: If, for ten million eons, one practices the ten paths of virtuous action, Yet generates a desire for the state of an Arhat or a Pratyekabuddha, At that moment, one’s ethical discipline is flawed and has degenerated; That generation of such a thought is far weightier than even a formal defeat.
gm: Even if one practices the ten paths of virtuous action for ten million aeons, If one generates the desire for the state of an arhat or solitary realizer, At that time, one's discipline becomes flawed and one's discipline degenerates; Generating that mind is much heavier even than a defeat.

dm: While guarding ethical discipline and fully dedicating it to supreme awakening, One is without conceit and does not praise oneself; One has completely abandoned the perception of a self and the perception of sentient beings; Such a bodhisattva is said to abide in the perfection of ethical discipline.
gm: Guarding discipline and completely dedicating it to supreme awakening, Without conceit about it and without praising oneself, Completely abandoning the perception of "I" and the perception of sentient beings— Such a bodhisattva is said to abide in the perfection of discipline.

dm: If a bodhisattva practicing the path of the Victors thinks, "These sentient beings are ethical, but those are unethical," Engaging in such diverse perceptions, they are utterly lacking in ethical discipline; Their morality has degenerated, and they lack completely purified morality.
gm: If a bodhisattva practicing the path of the Victorious Ones Thinks, "These sentient beings have discipline; these have broken discipline," By engaging in such diverse perceptions, their discipline is completely broken; Their discipline degenerates, and they lack completely pure discipline.

dm: For one who has no perception of a self or perception of a sentient being, And whose perceptions are free from attachment, how could there be a lack of restraint? One who has no conceit regarding restraint or lack of restraint— This is what the Guide has called the restraint of morality.
gm: Whoever has no perception of self and no perception of sentient beings, Being free from attachment to perceptions, how could they have non-restraint? Whoever has no conceit regarding restraint and non-restraint, This was taught by the Guide to be the discipline of restraint.

dm: Any pure being who possesses such morality as this, Is without bias toward anything pleasant or unpleasant. They give away their heads, hands, and feet without a trace of discouragement; They give away all their possessions, remaining forever free from attachment.
gm: Any pure sentient being who thus possesses discipline Has no view of anything as pleasant or unpleasant. Giving away their head, hands, and feet, they have no shrinking mind; Giving away all their possessions, they are always free from clinging.

dm: Having realized that all phenomena are by nature selfless and insubstantial, If they can give away even their own flesh without a discouraged mind, Then at that time, what need is there to mention the giving of external objects? If they were to be stingy, it would be impossible.
gm: Knowing that all dharmas are by nature selfless and insubstantial, If they give away even their own flesh without a shrinking mind, Then what need is there to mention giving away external objects? For them to act with miserliness is impossible.

dm: Those who grasp at the actual perception of a self and hold things as "mine" are attached; How could fools like these ever have the intention to give? Those who are stingy will be born in the realm of hungry ghosts; Even if they are born as humans, they will be destitute at that time.
gm: Perceiving a self, one is attached to things through grasping them as "mine"; How could fools have the mind of generosity? Miserly ones will be born in the realm of hungry ghosts; Or even if they are born as humans, they will then be impoverished.

dm: At that time, the bodhisattva, knowing that sentient beings are impoverished, Will take delight in generosity and always give with great excellence. They feel more joy from giving away the four continents, beautifully adorned, as if they were a glob of spittle, Than they would from acquiring those continents.
gm: Then, the bodhisattva, knowing that sentient beings are impoverished, Becomes intent on giving and always gives freely. The four continents, beautifully adorned, are like a glob of spit; Having given them away they become joyful, but attaining the continents is not like that.

dm: The wise and luminous bodhisattva, thinking, "May this gift be given To all sentient beings throughout the three realms of existence," Bestows the gift, and having done so, Dedicates it to supreme enlightenment for the benefit of all beings.
gm: The wise and brilliant bodhisattva, [thinking], "Of the three states of existence, To all those sentient beings, however many there are, may this gift Be given!" Having thought thus, they give gifts, And also dedicate them to supreme awakening for the sake of beings.

dm: Having given a gift, one does not dwell upon it as a substantial thing; One never has any expectation for its karmic maturation. Those who are skilled in giving in such a way give everything; By giving even a small amount, it becomes vast and immeasurable.
gm: Having given gifts, they do not abide in entities; They never have hope for a ripening result; Thus, being wise in giving, they let go of everything; Having given a little, it becomes much, immeasurable.

dm: However many sentient beings there are without exception throughout the three realms of existence, If one were to take all of them as a basis for consideration, and if all of them, To the Knowers of the World—the Buddhas, Arhats, and Pratyekabuddhas— Were to give gifts for infinite eons while seeking the excellence of a Śrāvaka,
gm: However many sentient beings there are without exception in the three states of existence, Taking them fully into consideration, if all of them To the Knowers of the World, the Buddhas, Arhats, and Pratyekabuddhas Give gifts for infinite eons, and properly seek the śrāvaka path—

dm: Yet a wise bodhisattva with skillful means Were to rejoice in the substance of those meritorious deeds, And fully dedicate it toward supreme, sublime enlightenment for the sake of sentient beings, By that complete dedication, one will outshine all living beings.
gm: Whatever wise bodhisattva, skilled in means, Rejoices in their bases of meritorious actions, And fully dedicates them to supreme awakening for the sake of beings, By fully dedicating them, they outshine all beings.

dm: Even a massive heap of ordinary glass trinkets Is outshone by a single precious lapis lazuli gem; Likewise, all the vast heaps of generosity of all beings Are outshone by a bodhisattva who rejoices.
gm: Even a great heap of imitation glass jewels Is completely outshone by a single precious lapis lazuli; Likewise, all the vast heaps of giving of all beings Are outshone by the rejoicing bodhisattva.

dm: If a bodhisattva, having given a gift to living beings, Does not regard it as their own and has no attachment to the object, From that, the roots of virtue will grow to have great power, Like the bright orb of the waxing moon in a cloudless sky.
gm: If the bodhisattva, having given gifts to beings, Does not make them "mine" and is unsparing of entities, Their roots of virtue will increase with great power, Like the radiant, cloudless moon disk in the waxing fortnight.

dm: Teaching of the gradual path
gm: Teaching on the Gradual Approach

dm: The sixth chapter explains the gradual path. Through the generosity of a bodhisattva, the path to the realm of hungry spirits is cut off; It likewise eliminates poverty and all afflictions. When practiced, one will obtain an infinite expansion of resources; Through generosity, one brings sentient beings who are suffering to full maturity.
gm: Chapter Six: Teaching the Gradual Training. By the bodhisattva's giving, the destiny of hungry ghosts is cut off; Poverty and likewise all afflictions are cut off; While practicing, they will obtain infinite, abundant wealth, And by giving, they fully ripen sentient beings who are suffering.

dm: Through ethical discipline, one abandons the various states of animal existence, And by abandoning the eight unfree states, one always finds leisure. Through patience, one will attain a sublime, vast, and beautiful form; With a lovely golden complexion, one becomes worthy of being beheld by all beings.
gm: By discipline, the nature of the manifold destinies of animals and The eight unfree states are abandoned, and leisure is always found. By patience, a fine, supreme, and vast form will be obtained, Golden-colored, beautiful, and worthy to be looked at by beings.

dm: Through diligence, virtuous qualities will not decline; One will find the treasury of the Victors, which is infinite primordial wisdom. Through meditative concentration, one abandons the base qualities of sensual desire; One fully accomplishes knowledge, supernormal powers, and meditative absorption.
gm: By diligence, pure qualities will not diminish, And infinite pristine wisdom, the treasury of the Victors, will be found. By concentration, the despised qualities of desire are discarded, And knowledge, superknowledges, and samadhi are accomplished.

dm: Through wisdom, one thoroughly understands the nature of phenomena, And will perfectly transcend the three realms without exception. Having turned the precious wheel, that preeminent leader among men Teaches the Dharma to beings in order to bring suffering to an end.
gm: By wisdom, having fully known the nature of phenomena, One will completely transcend the three realms without exception; The supreme leader of humans, having turned the precious wheel, Teaches the Dharma to beings in order to exhaust suffering.

dm: Teaching of complete enlightenment in a single instant
gm: Teaching on the Complete Awakening in a Single Moment

dm: The seventh chapter: teaching the attainment of complete enlightenment in a single instant. Having brought these phenomena to full completion, that bodhisattva,
gm: Chapter Seven: Teaching Complete Awakening in a Single Moment. Having fully perfected these dharmas, that bodhisattva

dm: Teaching of the Dharmakāya
gm: Teaching on the Dharmakāya

dm: The eighth chapter: teaching the Dharmakāya. One fully embraces the pure realm and the purity of sentient beings; One fully embraces the lineage of the Buddha and the lineage of the Dharma; Likewise, one fully embraces the lineage of the Saṅgha and all phenomena.
gm: Chapter Eight: Teaching the Dharmakāya. Fully upholds perfectly pure fields and pure sentient beings; Fully upholds the Buddha lineage and also the Dharma lineage; Likewise fully upholds the Sangha lineage and all dharmas.

dm: As the supreme physician who heals the ailments of wandering beings, He has spoken this teaching on wisdom, which possesses the path to enlightenment; This path to awakening is titled "The Collection of Precious Qualities," And is taught so that all sentient beings may attain it.
gm: By the supreme physician who heals the diseases of beings, This teaching of wisdom, endowed with the path to awakening, was taught; Its name is the Collection of Precious Qualities, the path to awakening; This path was explained in order for all sentient beings to obtain it.

dm: May the Noble Verses Summarizing the Perfection of Wisdom be complete.
gm: The Noble Verses on the Collection of the Perfection of Wisdom is complete.
